title: Janata
draft: Claude's draft 2026-10-17 from story_script_v1 §7 (4.0: walk out; locked down, not empty; shutters, police tape, a lone BMTC bus parked diagonally; the scooter gone from hospital parking; phone: UPI dead, Maps cached, Chats one tick [C]), ADR-10 (a locked-down city, Janata Curfew memory, treated with respect, no real dates or leaders), chapter_board_merge §B2 (4a inflation, barricaded shops selling through a slot) + Act 4 systems plan v1 (approved 'default', 2026-10-17) §8 Q3 (UPI flickers until the hill) and Q5 (travel told by cards), profile doc §4 (the ID card as a lockdown pass), 3.5's leaving card (holds on CURFEW until this pocket exists), ADR-117 (real streets via OSM; the hospital stays fictional). The user edits the words and numbers; then it is built after S2.
time: Act 4 day 0 — Thursday, 08:30, straight after 3.5's leaving card
player_goal: Get out of Hebbal and start for home — the hill at Ambedkar Nagar, across the city.
design_goal: The city is not empty, it is shut: people behind grilles and balconies, nobody on the road. Every system the player learned in Acts 0–2 answers wrongly — UPI says 'Server busy', Maps shows yesterday, Chats deliver one tick, no auto stops, the bus is parked across the road. No infected are seen: 4.0 is dread, 4.1 is the run. Calm surface, Curious underneath (ADR-24).

entry.note: card_leaving_ward gets a `then` to this pocket and sets `act4` (Act 4 day 0 starts here)

cast.role: NEW. A constable at a steel barricade with a register. Checks your ID card (the 'Aadhaar-ish' game ID from the starter kit) and the discharge slip: 'Where are you going?' — 'Home.' — 'Then go straight there. Stay inside after five.' The second person to say 'five' without saying why.

NEW. A medical-and-provisions store with its shutter three-quarters down; a hand through the gap. Water ₹60 (was ₹20), biscuits ₹90. UPI: 'Server busy' first, then it goes through. 'Cash is better. Nobody has cash.'

NEW. An old man on a first-floor balcony with a steel tumbler of coffee who watches you walk the whole length of the street and says nothing until you look up: 'You're from the hospital?' — and goes inside.

beats.what: The hospital steps, 08:30. Bright, quiet. The ambulance bay empty. The two-wheeler parking: a row of bikes under dust covers — your bay has only the chain lock on the ground (the wreck was taken, or Sameer's bike was collected; the line follows 3.1's flag). The phone in your bag: 7 % battery.

The phone, opened for the first time in Act 4 (phone: Act 4 state as data — 'network' token): UPI 'Server busy · try later'; Maps opens on a grey 'Showing saved map' banner with yesterday's pins; Chats — your messages to Amma show one tick; Calls 'Network busy'; News: the last push, 'CURFEW: stay indoors. Essential services only.'; Reels: the last clip loops. Battery drains while it is open.

The street: shutters down on every shop, police tape across a lane mouth, a BMTC bus parked diagonally across two lanes with its doors open and nobody in it (step in: the ticket machine's screen still on), a dog asleep in the middle of the road, laundry still on a line. The constable at the barricade checks your ID and slip (F3a). People only behind things: grilles, balconies, a half-open door that closes as you pass.

The slot shop (optional, the first Act 4 purchase): the price is three times, UPI fails once and goes through on the second try (4a inflation, plan Q3). Water ₹60, biscuits ₹90. This is the last place money works until the hill.

The end of the street: no autos at the stand (one auto with its hood tied down). A card: the walk — the Hebbal flyover empty in both directions, Mekhri Circle, a milk van that gives you a lift as far as Shivajinagar ('Don't tell anyone I stopped'), the long walk east, a man hosing a temple's steps who stops to watch you pass. It lands in Indiranagar at 16:40 (4.1).

economy.note: 4a inflation: 3× the Act 1 price; UPI fails once first
